title: A locally finite type algebraic-space map with open diagonal is unramified
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to Y$ a locally finite type morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $\Delta_{X/Y}:X\to X\times_YX$ is an open immersion. Then $f$ is unramified. The fibre product is the sheaf fibre product, open immersion means that every scheme base change is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and unramifiedness is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (2). The reverse implication is already represented by lem-sfb-unramified-space-open-diagonal when the target is a scheme.

proof.text: Use the chart convention in the statement explicitly: for every commutative square $fa=bh$ with schemes $U,V$, representable etale maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, and $h:U\to V$, local finite type of $f$ means local finite type of $h$ in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; unramifiedness means unramifiedness of these scheme maps in [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. These are the chart definitions of Tags 03XF and 03ZH, using the all-diagrams condition of 03MJ. Fix any such square. We will prove its $h$ unramified. No surjectivity of these particular charts is required.

Put $Q=X\times_YX$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and $P=U\times_YU$. The scheme-source fibre-product clause of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] makes $P$ a scheme. The map $P\to Q$ factors as $U\times_YU\to X\times_YU\to X\times_YX$. The first arrow is the base change of $a$ along $X\times_YU\to X$ (first projection), and the second is the base change of $a$ along $X\times_YX\to X$ (second projection). Both are representable etale, hence so is their composite, by the base-change and composition clauses of that same node. The pullback identifications are $U\times_X(X\times_YU)\simeq U\times_YU$ and $(X\times_YX)\times_XU\simeq X\times_YU$, respectively; each forgets the repeated $X$ coordinate, with inverse inserting $a(u)$.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), diagram: product of source charts; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03EC and representable scheme tests.

proof.text: Set $E=V\times_YV$ and $D=U\times_VU$, both schemes by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Since $b$ is representable etale, $E\to V\to Y$ is representable etale by base change and composition. The diagonal $V\to E$ is therefore etale by the comparison clause of that node, applied to the two schemes $V,E$ etale over $Y$. The map $P\to E$ sends $(u_1,u_2)$ to $(h(u_1),h(u_2))$. The square with top row $D\to V$, bottom row $P\to E$, and right arrow $V\to E$ is cartesian: explicitly $D=P\times_E V$, on each test scheme a point of $P\times_E V$ is $(u_1,u_2,v)$ with $h(u_1)=v=h(u_2)$. Forgetting $v$ gives a point of $D$. Conversely, a point $(u_1,u_2)$ of $D$ gives a point of $P$ because $fa=bh$ implies $fa(u_1)=fa(u_2)$, and inserting $v=h(u_1)=h(u_2)$ gives a point of $P\times_E V$. These operations are mutually inverse and natural, proving the claimed sheaf isomorphism. Thus $D\to P$ is representable etale by base change. Composing with Step 2 gives a representable etale map $D\to Q$.

source.place: Tag 05W1, cartesian right square and middle vertical arrow; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03EC (lemma-etale-over-space)(2).

proof.text: The assumed open immersion $\Delta_f:X\to Q$ is representable etale: each scheme base change is an open immersion and hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). Consequently $U\xrightarrow{a}X\xrightarrow{\Delta_f}Q$ is representable etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The diagonal $\delta=\Delta_h:U\to D$ satisfies $(D\to Q)\delta=\Delta_f a$: on each test scheme both maps send $u$ to $(a(u),a(u))$. The comparison clause of the same node, applied to the schemes $U,D$ representable etale over the algebraic space $Q$, now proves that $\delta$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 05W1(2), etaleness of the chart diagonal; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03EC(2).

proof.text: The map $\delta:U\to U\times_VU$ is a monomorphism: equality of $\delta r$ and $\delta s$ implies $r=s$ by composing with either projection. Its etaleness from Step 4 gives flatness and local finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The scheme criterion [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open] therefore makes $\delta$ an open immersion. Together with local finite type of $h$ from Step 1, [def-weil-unramified-morphism] says exactly that $h$ is unramified. As the chart square was arbitrary, the chart convention in Step 1 gives unramifiedness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 05W1(2), final implication; etale.tex Tag 025G (theorem-etale-radicial-open)(3) implies (1); morphisms.tex Tag 02GE(2).

proof_origin.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (2). The final etale-monomorphism step is expanded using etale.tex Tag 025G, avoiding the unneeded assertion that every scheme diagonal is globally an immersion.
